summary:
FSD (Supervised) is a subscription in the U.S.: Tesla lists $99 a month and no longer sells it outright [2][3]. Tesla reported 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of Q3, counting earlier lifetime purchases [4].

The current software is FSD v14.3.13 on AI4 cars and v14.3 Lite on HW3, now in update 2026.38.5.11, which began a wider rollout on October 24 [1][19]. HW3 still won't get unsupervised FSD [5]. Tesla's manuals have quietly renamed the computers: AI4 is now "SI4" and HW3 "SI3" [21]. Tesla's target for unsupervised FSD in owners' cars is Q2 2027, inside Robotaxi zones first [5][6].

Robotaxi runs with no one on board in six metros, and Houston's zone grew roughly tenfold this week to an estimated 254 square miles [14][23]. Texas registrations reached 1,080 robotaxis, more than half Cybercabs [24]. Federal crash reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi incidents in Austin since July 2025, against 188 for Waymo since 2023 [25].

Latvia became the 10th European country to approve the system, sold there as Tesla Assisted Driving, with rollout "soon" [20]. In the U.S., Turo now shows renters which Teslas have verified FSD [22]. In South Korea, police booked 80 people for illegally unlocking FSD on cars not approved for it [26].

price.purchase: Can't be bought outright: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) is subscription-only [2]. The $8,000 one-time purchase ended after February 14, 2026 [3].
price.note: FSD bought outright by an earlier owner stays with the car unless it was transferred away before March 31, 2026; a previous owner's subscription does not carry over, and Luxe Package FSD may carry over depending on when it was bought [2].

versions.note: First out in 2026.38.5.10 on October 20; the 2026.38.5.11 point release began rolling October 24 and reached about 10% of cars by October 26. Rewritten AI compiler, vision-encoder upgrades and Automatic Collision Evasion [1][19]. Tesla's manuals now call this computer SI4 [21].

Distilled from v14 for HW3: parking, unparking, reversing, Arrival Options and Speed Profiles at all times, including a new SLOTH profile; 2026.38.5.11 has reached some 2020-and-older HW3 Model S and X [1][19].

hardware.fsd: None as built: HW2 is not FSD capable [13].
hardware.note: HW2 went into S and X from October 2016 to about August 2017; S/X built earlier in 2016 have the older Autopilot 1 hardware and no FSD path [13].

hardware.fsd: None as built; runs FSD (Supervised) only if the computer was retrofitted to HW3, which Tesla did free for owners who had bought FSD [13].
hardware.note: HW2.5 from about August 2017 to March 2019; 2017 is a split year with HW2. Check the Autopilot computer line in Additional Vehicle Information [12][13].

hardware.fsd: FSD (Supervised) v14.3 Lite [1]; Tesla has said HW3 will not run unsupervised FSD [5].
hardware.note: HW3 from March 22, 2019 [13]; 2019 is a split year with HW2.5 and 2023 a split year with AI4 (cars bought after March 2023 likely AI4) [12].

check: In the car: Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information shows the Autopilot computer (2.5, 3 or 4); this needs software 2024.38 or later [12].
Controls > Software also shows whether Full Self-Driving Capability is in the car's included package [2].
Front cameras: AI4 cars show two red lenses and one black dummy lens; AI4 side repeaters have a red tint [12].
Build date: S/X after about March 2023, U.S. Model Y after late May 2023 and the 2024 Model 3 are likely AI4 [12].
Tesla's owner's manuals now call the computer the "SI Computer": HW3 is listed as SI3 and AI4 as SI4. Same hardware, new name [21].
transfer: You can no longer move FSD to another car or account: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Transfer Program ended on March 31, 2026 [2][3]. If you sell a car whose FSD was bought outright, the purchase stays with that car, so the next owner gets it [2]. If you had a subscription, it ends with your ownership and the buyer must subscribe on their own Tesla account [2]. Owners who bought FSD before the change keep it on the car permanently, but a new Tesla means a new $99 subscription [3]. We found no current transfer offer; the Tesla app 4.62 adds FSD referral rewards, which are not a transfer [18].

robotaxi.status: No one on board; Cybercabs in the fleet; geofence expanded to Circuit of the Americas for the Grand Prix [9][14]; NHTSA reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi crashes in Austin since July 2025 (25 Model Y, 1 Cybercab) [25]. Texas registrations: 1,080 robotaxis, 573 of them Cybercabs, not all in service [24]
No one on board; Cybercab rides due in November [6][14]

Safety driver required by California rules; not driverless [5][7]

buying: Check Controls > Software for Full Self-Driving Capability: only an outright purchase stays with the car [2].
Don't count on moving FSD from your old car; transfers ended March 31, 2026 [2].
Prefer AI4: HW3 gets the Lite build and won't run unsupervised FSD [1][5].
On a 2017-2019 S/X or early Model 3, confirm the computer is HW3 or later, not HW2/HW2.5 [12][13].
Budget $99 a month if the car has no purchased FSD [2].
Want to try it first? From October 28 Turo shows U.S. renters which Teslas have verified FSD (Supervised) [22].
Outside the U.S., don't buy a car with an aftermarket FSD unlock: Korean police booked 80 people for using such devices, which carry up to two years in prison there [26].
changes: Update 2026.38.5.11 (FSD v14.3.13 on AI4, v14.3 Lite on HW3) began a wider rollout on October 24 [19].
Latvia approved FSD (Supervised), sold in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving: the 10th European country [20].
Tesla's owner's manuals renamed the computers: AI4 is now SI4, HW3 is SI3 [21].
Houston's Robotaxi zone grew about tenfold, to an estimated 254 square miles [23]; Texas registrations reached 1,080 robotaxis, more than half Cybercabs [24].
Turo began labelling rentals with verified FSD on October 28; eligible hosts get a free month [22].
NHTSA data: 249 robotaxi incidents in Austin since 2023, 26 of them Tesla's, 14 people with alleged minor injuries [25].
Seoul police booked 80 people for illegal FSD unlock devices on cars not approved for it [26].

pt.summary:
O FSD (Supervised) é vendido por assinatura nos EUA: a Tesla cobra US$ 99 por mês e não o vende mais à vista [2][3]. A Tesla relatou 1,74 milhão de assinaturas ativas do FSD no fim do terceiro trimestre, contando compras vitalícias anteriores [4].

O software atual é o FSD v14.3.13 nos carros AI4 e o v14.3 Lite no HW3, agora na atualização 2026.38.5.11, que começou a chegar a mais carros em 24 de outubro [1][19]. O HW3 continua sem previsão de FSD não supervisionado [5]. Os manuais da Tesla renomearam os computadores: o AI4 agora é "SI4" e o HW3, "SI3" [21]. A meta da Tesla para o FSD não supervisionado nos carros dos donos é o segundo trimestre de 2027, primeiro dentro das zonas do Robotaxi [5][6].

O Robotaxi roda sem ninguém a bordo em seis regiões metropolitanas, e a zona de Houston cresceu cerca de dez vezes nesta semana, para cerca de 254 milhas quadradas [14][23]. Os registros do Texas chegaram a 1.080 robotáxis, mais da metade Cybercabs [24]. Relatórios federais listam 26 incidentes com robotáxis da Tesla em Austin desde julho de 2025, contra 188 da Waymo desde 2023 [25].

A Letônia foi o 10º país europeu a aprovar o sistema, vendido lá como Tesla Assisted Driving, com lançamento "em breve" [20]. Nos EUA, a Turo agora mostra quais Teslas para alugar têm FSD verificado [22]. Na Coreia do Sul, a polícia indiciou 80 pessoas por desbloquear ilegalmente o FSD em carros não aprovados [26].

de.summary:
FSD (Supervised) gibt es in den USA nur im Abo: Tesla verlangt 99 Dollar im Monat und verkauft es nicht mehr zum Festpreis [2][3]. Tesla meldete zum Ende des dritten Quartals 1,74 Millionen aktive FSD-Abos, frühere Einmalkäufe eingerechnet [4].

Aktuell laufen FSD v14.3.13 auf AI4-Autos und v14.3 Lite auf HW3, jetzt im Update 2026.38.5.11, das seit dem 24. Oktober breiter verteilt wird [1][19]. HW3 bekommt weiterhin kein unbeaufsichtigtes FSD [5]. Teslas Handbücher haben die Computer umbenannt: AI4 heißt jetzt "SI4", HW3 "SI3" [21]. Tesla peilt unbeaufsichtigtes FSD in Kundenautos für das zweite Quartal 2027 an, zuerst in den Robotaxi-Zonen [5][6].

Robotaxi fährt in sechs Großräumen ohne Person an Bord, und die Zone in Houston wuchs diese Woche etwa auf das Zehnfache, auf geschätzt 254 Quadratmeilen [14][23]. In Texas sind 1.080 Robotaxis zugelassen, mehr als die Hälfte Cybercabs [24]. Bundesberichte verzeichnen in Austin seit Juli 2025 26 Vorfälle mit Tesla-Robotaxis, gegenüber 188 bei Waymo seit 2023 [25].

Lettland hat das System als zehntes europäisches Land zugelassen, dort als Tesla Assisted Driving verkauft, Start "bald" [20]. In den USA zeigt Turo jetzt, welche Mietteslas verifiziertes FSD haben [22]. In Südkorea zeigte die Polizei 80 Personen an, die FSD auf nicht zugelassenen Autos illegal freigeschaltet hatten [26].
